title: The way to the far shore
hookLine: sixteen young brahmins bring their questions, and each is answered

lines: AN OLD TEACHER BY THE GODAVARI.
cards: Far to the south, on the banks of the Godavari river, an old brahmin teacher named Bavari is living quietly when a visitor arrives, demands money, and, when Bavari has none to give, curses him: in seven days your head will split in seven pieces.
Bavari is shaken. A kindly spirit tells him that the visitor knows nothing about heads splitting, but that someone in the north does know: a Buddha. Bavari doesn't go himself.
He sends his sixteen students instead.

teach.b: The prologue to the Sutta Nipata's fifth chapter traces their road north town by town, until they find the Buddha at a rocky shrine near Rajagaha.
They ask Bavari's questions first, about the head and its splitting, and the Buddha answers that ignorance is the head, and knowledge, with faith, mindfulness and effort, is what splits it.
Then each of the sixteen asks his own. Ajita asks what the world is wrapped in. Mettagu asks where suffering comes from.
Upasiva asks what to lean on to cross. Hemaka, Todeyya, Kappa, Mogharaja: each brings something real, and each gets an answer shaped to him. That's the striking thing about this chapter.
It isn't one teaching to a crowd. It's sixteen conversations. The word that names it, parayana, means the way to the beyond, the going to the far shore.
And the image running through it is a flood: the rushing water of craving and views that has to be crossed.
At the end, Pingiya, old and frail by his own account, goes home and sings the Buddha's praise to Bavari.
The week behind: the dart of grief, only by deeds, the axe in the mouth, deep rivers are quiet, no view to cling to, fear from the rod. Now sixteen questions, and a river to cross.

how: The Parayanavagga is studied in Theravada monasteries and often taught one question at a time; its image of crossing the flood to the far shore runs through Buddhist chanting and teaching.

games.q: the way to the far shore: tap the pairs.
p: the old teacher by the Godavari
went home and sang the praise

s: Bavari made the journey north himself
he stayed by the Godavari and sent his sixteen students.
each of the sixteen asks his own question
the chapter is sixteen conversations, one for each student.
parayana means the way to the far shore
the going to the beyond, the crossing of the flood.

games.q: you're Bavari, old and frightened by a curse. a spirit tells you there is a Buddha far in the north. what do you do?
o: ignore it and wait out the seven days.
send your sixteen students, each with a question.
go after the man who cursed you.
games.why: he stays, and sends his students. the questions they bring back fill the whole last chapter of the Sutta Nipata.

practice: If you had walked that far to ask one question, what would it be? Not a clever one, but the one that's actually there, under the others.
Let it come slowly, and when it does, don't answer it; just hold it, the way the students held theirs on the road.

wordCard.voice: Parayana. The way to the far shore, the last chapter of the Sutta Nipata, where sixteen students each ask their question.

orig.note: Pali parayana: the way to the beyond, the going to the far shore. the name of Sn 5.

carryVoice: Your line: crossing the flood. A real question is worth the walk. Another week, complete.
